angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,367,746 km at 969.09 pc = 0.02 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 1.0319 +/- 0.0121 mas (same row, RUWE 1.01): 969.09 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.966 +/- 0.013 solar radii from Esteves et al. 2015, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of Kepler-7 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...804..150E/abstract): 1,367,746 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.359 +/- 0.031 solar masses from Esteves et al. 2015, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of Kepler-7 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...804..150E/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5933 +/- 44 K from Esteves et al. 2015, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-7 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...804..150E/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Esteves et al. 2015, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-7 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...804..150E/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/kepler-7.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 3.984, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
